To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we developed a machine learning algorithm to identify adjuvant specific signatures in human vaccine induced responses; (ii) we identified immune signatures that distinguish vaccine induced immune responses to two similar adjuvants; and (iii) we demonstrated that the combination of machine learning and high content profiling is a useful strategy for identifying adjuvant effects on vaccine immunogenicity.
the combination of immunoprofiling and computational analysis of human vaccine induced immune responses is a powerful approach to identify subtle adjuvant mediated effects on immunity.

we have developed a computational approach to identify immune signatures of vaccine induced immunity, that these signatures can be used to predict adjuvant effects, and that these signatures can identify unexpected immune responses induced by the vaccine.

the development of a novel computational framework for the analysis of vaccine induced immunity and its application to a clinically relevant adjuvant selection problem.
the identification of immunological signatures that can be utilized to predict the impact of different adjuvant formulations on the immune response to a vaccine.
identifying the effects of aduivant formulation and composition on vaccine induced immunity, which is critical for the rational selection of adjuvants for future vaccine design.

the adjuvants have a subtle impact on the immune responses induced by a subunit vaccine, but that this subtle impact is sufficient to distinguish adjuvants by a machine learning approach.

we have demonstrated that immunoprofiling and machine learning can be used to identify subtle differences in vaccine induced immunity.

adjuvants produce subtle, but distinct, effects on vaccine immunogenicity, that can be identified by in depth immunoprofiling and machine learning, and that can be leveraged in the rational design of future vaccines.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the subtle effects of adjuvants on vaccine induced immunity can be identified using a combination of immunoprofiling and machine learning, and these effects can be used to inform rational vaccine design.

the combination of immunoprofiling and machine learning is able to identify subtle, but statistically significant, adjuvant specific differences that may be missed by traditional vaccine evaluation approaches.

immunoprofiling combined with machine learning can identify adjuvant specific signatures in human vaccine induced immunity that are subtle but nonetheless critical for adjuvant selection and vaccine efficacy.
